newsitem.title: USA: U.S. April consumer credit up $7.6 bln.
newsitem.headline: U.S. April consumer credit up $7.6 bln.

text.p: U.S. consumer installment credit rose in April by $7.6 billion, or a 7.6 percent annual rate, following a revised $3.1 billion increase in March at a three percent rate, the Federal Reserve said on Frinesday.
The April rise in consumer credit was the largest monthly increase since a $10.3-billion jump in January and was much stronger than Wall Street economists' forecasts for a $4.3-billion rise.
Previously, the Fed said March consumer credit had grown by $2 billion but it revised that estimate up significantly.

Auto credit outstanding shot up $4 billion at a 12.7 percent annual rate in April after shrinking in March by $900 million at a 2.7 percent annual rate. It was the biggest monthly increase in outstanding auto loans since they climbed by $5.5-billion last July.
Revolving, or credit-card, credit rose by $1.8 billion at a 4.3 percent annual rate in April, the Fed said. Credit-card debt had risen $1.5 billion at a 3.9 percent rate in March.

Other credit, which includes consumer bank loans like those for mobile homes and to pay for education but not real estate mortgages, rose by $2 billion at a 6.6 percent annual rate in April. In March, this category of credit was up $2.4 billion at an eight percent annual rate.
Before seasonal adjustment, total outstanding consumer credit in April was $1.209 trillion, up from $1.131 trillion a year earlier in April 1996.
